findings.title: The MCY 2003 Case 1 tables come from a truncated series and are off by up to 0.86 % of the rise, over 4x the 0.2 % pass threshold. F1's two reference checks contradict each other.
findings.detail: The paper says its tables use 50 terms in each sum (Maple). For Case 1a (300x300x10 mm plate, k=10, h=10, 25 mm sources) 50 terms is far from converged. The converged series gives centroid temperatures of 85.45 / 109.15 °C; the paper prints 84.97 / 108.43 °C. That is 0.80 % and 0.86 % of the 60 / 84 K rise. The source means are also low by 0.26–0.27 %. Three independent methods all sit above the printed values: the converged series, my graded finite-volume solve and Culham's least-squares result quoted in the same paper (85.95 / 109.92). The draft does not say whether dT_analytic is the tabulated value or the converged series, and both readings break. (a) If the converged series is the reference (F1: doubling the terms changes the value by < 1e-6), F1's other check fails: the series must reproduce the published tables to their printed digits, and it does not for Cases 1a, 1b or 2 (Case 2 centroid 103.796 vs a printed 103.82). Only Case 3 passes. That check is gated as an experimental failure, so E006 is invalid by construction. (b) If the tabulated values are the reference, a correct solver scores about 0.86 % on Case 1a. That is between A1 (0.2 %) and K1 (1 %), so the result is inconclusive, which the draft treats as a fail, and decision_if_fail wrongly moves the reference to scikit-fem. The scikit-fem fallback would hit the same problem. Either way the claim that the thresholds and the cases can resolve the decision does not hold as written.
findings.evidence: My own series (surface mode amplitude q_mn·Z(β), with Z from an N-layer tanh recursion). Validation: at 50 terms it reproduces the Case 3 printed values (80.615 / 78.871 vs 80.61 / 78.87), and its converged Case 2 centroids (97.388 / 103.796 / 101.263 / 99.920) match the literature note's scikit-fem run (97.388 / 103.797 / 101.264 / 99.921) to 1e-3 K. Case 1a centroids at M=50 vs M=1600: 84.939 vs 85.451 and 108.384 vs 109.153. Graded-grid FV of Case 1a at 1.0 and 0.5 mm, source means: 80.866 → 80.785 and 102.257 → 102.136. Richardson extrapolation gives 80.704 / 102.015, against the converged series' 80.705 / 102.017 and the printed 80.56 / 101.81.
findings.suggested_check: Define dT_ref as the converged series. Check it against the tables only by reproducing them with the paper's own 50-term truncation (or within a stated tolerance), and record the paper's truncation bias per case before registering E006.

findings.title: Normalising by the total rise above the fluid hides most of the spreading error; O002 judges die-local rise, pair differences and spread
findings.detail: In MCY Case 2 the 1D term (film plus slab, which any energy-conserving solver gets right) is 71.87 K of a 72.4–78.8 K rise. The spreading part is only 0.52–6.93 K. A 0.2 % tolerance on the rise therefore allows 2.3–28 % error in the spreading part and ±0.15 K per source on a 6.4 K spread between sources. O002 measures Tj max against the die-local rise (A3), pair differences in K (A2) and spread (A4/A5). A1 as written verifies the quantity those criteria remove. The draft also does not define what 'rise' is measured from in the manufactured-solution cases, and a large offset there would dilute the error the same way.
findings.evidence: Case 2 decomposition from the converged series. Spreading part: src1 0.521 K (0.7 % of the rise), src2 6.929 K (8.8 %), src3 4.396 K (5.8 %), src4 3.054 K (4.1 %). 0.2 % of the rise is 0.145–0.158 K.
findings.suggested_check: Add a criterion on the spreading part (θ − θ_1D) or on the differences between sources, or normalise by the die-local rise as O002's A3 does.

findings.title: No 3D analytic case covers the default stack plus die attach and SiC die; the N-layer case D0006 requires is dropped
findings.detail: scope_in claims verification 'in the default DBC stack plus die attach and SiC die'. The MCY 2003 cases have at most two layers (Case 1b), 2–10 mm thick, and the only multilayer case is the 1D series. A conforming finite-volume scheme with harmonic-mean conductances solves that 1D case exactly on any grid, so it cannot discriminate. The thin (0.05–0.1 mm), high-contrast die-attach, die, Cu and Al2O3 layers, where 3D interface and lateral-conductance bugs would show, are never compared with an analytic solution. D0006 lists the Bagnall, Muzychka & Wang (2014) N-layer surface field for per-die maximum and spread. O002's A1, which is the same metric (E006.max_rel_err_vs_analytic), still says E006 includes it, so the two drafts disagree on what E006 contains. With perfect contact the N-layer case is the same Fourier series with a layer-impedance recursion (about 10 lines in my check), so cost does not justify dropping it.
findings.evidence: Draft hypothesis vs D0006 'Verification before any L1 comparison' vs O002 A1 description. The N-layer recursion I wrote reproduces Case 1b (two layers) to its printed digits at 50 terms (56.548 vs 56.55).
findings.suggested_check: Add an N-layer case on a laterally uniform default stack with die attach and die and die-sized sources, with the surface maximum and the spread taken from the full field.

findings.title: A1 is judged on one grid's point value; the three-grid estimate and observed order are only reported
findings.detail: F2 is meant to detect a 'lucky grid', but none of its checks are gated. A1 uses a single point value, observed order is reported only, and the response is 'refine; report'. Rows carry a grid column, but the draft does not say which grid's rows enter max_rel_err. If the rows from all three grids enter, the coarsest grid sets the verdict; if the author picks one, the result is a forking path. The energy-balance check cannot catch discretisation error, because a finite-volume scheme conserves energy by construction. My crude FV had |Q_out/Q_in − 1| ≈ 1e-13 while its error was 0.3 % of the rise.
findings.evidence: My Case 1a FV: energy balance −3.7e-13 at the coarse grid, with source-mean errors of 0.16–0.24 K that halve on refinement.
findings.suggested_check: Pin the grid that enters the metric to the finest grid. Require |err| plus the Richardson estimate ≤ 0.002 and an observed order inside a stated range.

findings.title: The k(T) manufactured-solution case has no null check against a constant-k solver
findings.detail: The draft does not fix how strongly k varies in the manufactured solution, or over what temperature range. If the manufactured temperature range times dk/dT is small, a solver that ignores k(T) meets the 0.2 % threshold, so the criterion would be met by a predictor that ignores the k(T) physics.
findings.evidence: Order-of-magnitude estimate: the constant-k error is about β·ΔT/2 of the rise, so with β ≈ 3e-3 /K (Al2O3) any manufactured rise under ~1.3 K passes with constant k.
findings.suggested_check: Require the constant-k solution to miss each k(T) manufactured case by at least 5x the A1 threshold before E006 is registered.

findings.title: The scope 'at grid resolutions the solver uses in O002' is undefined
findings.detail: O002's grid is not fixed yet, and the MCY geometries span 10–300 mm. O002-scale cells (~0.1 mm) on a 300 mm plate would mean tens of millions of unknowns. The phrase cannot be checked as written.
findings.suggested_check: State the grid per case, or a resolution rule in units of layer thickness and source size.

independent_checks_performed: Derived the MCY (2003) surface series myself (Laplace equation, Robin sink, uniform-flux top, adiabatic sides) and generalised it to N layers with a tanh impedance recursion. Validated it on the Case 3 printed values (80.61 / 78.87) and Case 1b (56.55) at 50 terms, and on the literature note's scikit-fem Case 2 centroids (agreement ≤ 1e-3 K).
Extracted Case 1–3 inputs and Tables 1, 3 and 4 from the UWaterloo PDF of the paper (doi:10.1115/1.1568125). The paper states 50 terms per sum, computed in Maple.
Term-doubling study for Case 2: the < 1e-6 relative-change criterion is reached at M≈1600–3200, so F1's convergence check is feasible.
Case 1a, 50-term vs converged series: the printed centroids are 0.80 % and 0.86 % of the rise below the converged values, and the printed means 0.26–0.27 % below.

Independent graded-grid finite-volume solve of Case 1a on two grids with Richardson extrapolation: source means 80.704 / 102.015, matching the converged series' 80.705 / 102.017 and confirming the tables are biased.
Split the Case 2 rise into the 1D term and the spreading part to measure how much the 0.2 % normalisation dilutes the spreading error.
Compared the O006 draft's hypothesis and A1 with the D0006 verification list, the O002 draft's A1 and F1, and mfos.metrics.max_rel_err (recomputable from rows; which grid enters is unspecified).
caveats: I read the paper's equations and tables from raw PDF text extraction. I could not reproduce the paper's Case 2 numbers exactly with 50 terms (differences ≤ 0.02 K), so its Maple evaluation probably differed slightly. This does not affect the Case 1a conclusion, which three independent methods support.
My finite-volume check is a crude scratch solver that converges at first order, used only to confirm the converged series. It says nothing about the in-house solver, which does not exist yet.

The blocker has a simple fix (define the reference as the converged series and record the paper's truncation bias). Once fixed, findings 2–4 remain as scope and evidence limits on what A1 verifies for O002.
